Rivers reclaim the city: how daylighted streams changed a neighbourhood

For decades the brook ran unseen beneath the high street, culverted in the 1950s and all but forgotten. This spring, contractors prised the road apart and let the water back into the light for the first time in seventy years.

Residents describe the change as immediate. Herons returned within weeks, and the cafes that once backed onto a car park now open their doors onto a shaded channel of moving water. Planners point to cooler summer temperatures and fewer flash floods downstream.

Critics caution that the scheme was expensive and that maintenance costs remain unclear, but few residents interviewed this week said they would trade the river back for the tarmac it replaced.
